judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives under the same 'Shapes' sub-theme of Mensuration and Geometry. The first asks pupils to identify the curved surfaces of a cylinder (Topic 1, three-dimensional shapes); the second asks pupils to indicate the square corner of a 2-dimensional shape (Topic 2, two-dimensional shapes). These are complementary shape-attribute identification skills (surfaces of 3D solids vs. corners of 2D figures) that reinforce recognition of geometric features, giving substantive conceptual coherence. However, they sit in different topics with no clear developmental dependency and share the same grade rank (1) with no substantive evidence that mastery of one supports success in the other, so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted. Nomination signals (token overlap of stem words like 'pupils should be able to', page proximity, shared ancestors) are generic and add no directional weight.

Understanding place value of tens and units substantively supports the ability to write two-digit numbers 1-99 correctly, giving a same-rank developmental direction from the place-value concept toward the writing skill. judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the shared 'Primary Measures' Sub-Theme within Mensuration and Geometry, but they sit under different Topics (Weight vs Length). The first compares the weights of common objects (light/heavy); the second applies length and ordering of lengths in the environment. They share substantive conceptual coherence as early measurement skills involving comparing/ordering objects by a measurable attribute, which reinforces general measurement reasoning without one being a dependency for the other. Both are at the same canonical rank (PRIMARY ONE), so no developmental direction is justified; token/page/rank proximity alone are not semantic evidence. This supports symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards.
